transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-11
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rajat Singh (Redwood SE), Dana Ortiz (Apogee - Head of Search), Leo Park (Apogee - ML Eng), Sofia Ruiz (Apogee - CTO)

Summary: quick intro, current infra, search pain points, vector DB & rerank approach, hosting decision criteria, next steps.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, this is Rajat our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Dana Ortiz: Good, thanks. Dana here. We, um, we've been evaluating vector approaches, excited to hear what Redwood recommends.
[00:15] Rajat Singh: Awesome. Quick agenda, we'll ask about your current stack, latency and cost targets, then discuss embedding dimensionality, vector db integration, and hosting (hosted/dedicated/private).
[00:26] Sofia Ruiz: Sounds good. We're on a tight timeline — Q3 launch for our new search product.
[00:31] Leo Park: Also to note, we have an existing Elasticsearch layer with BM25 and signals, we want to add semantic re-ranking, hybrid search is core.
[00:42] Maya Chen: Perfect, can you describe current throughput? QPS, doc count, average doc size?
[00:47] Dana Ortiz: Sure, baseline is about 150 qps peak, nightly indexing to around 8 million docs, average article ~1.2k tokens. For re-rank stage we only score top 200 candidates from BM25.
[01:05] Rajat Singh: So a typical flow would be BM25 to get top-k, then embed or fetch embeddings and run vector similarity/rerank. Two options: store pre-computed embeddings in your vector DB, or compute on the fly. Given 8M docs, pre-compute is standard.
[01:25] Leo Park: We're currently storing dense vectors in an Elastic plugin experiment, but it's pretty heavy. Considering Pinecone or Weaviate, and also evaluating FAISS in-house.
[01:34] Maya Chen: Totally. We see customers do both. Hosted Redwood can integrate with Pinecone/Weaviate or you can run Dedicated/Private where you host FAISS/HNSW on-prem or in their VPC. The big tradeoffs are latency predictability and throughput cost.
[01:51] Dana Ortiz: Can you unpack dimensionality? Our embeddings currently 1536 dims from an off-the-shelf model, but some teams suggest 768 to save space. What's Redwood's take?
[02:02] Rajat Singh: 1536 gives slightly better semantic fidelity for complex queries, but 768 often suffices and reduces storage and ANN compute. Also consider quantization (int8, product quant) and index type (HNSW vs IVF+PQ) — Dedicated gives you control to tune those kernels on GPU.
[02:20] Sofia Ruiz: Is there a rule of thumb for latency at rerank stage, given top-200 reranks?
[02:25] Rajat Singh: If you fetch precomputed vectors and run an ANN search for top-200, typical latencies are sub-50ms for the vector search on a tuned index for 8M vectors, but end-to-end rerank (including scoring, any cross-encoder) often lands 80-200ms depending on whether you run a cross-encoder for final rerank. On Hosted, we expose latency SLAs and can auto-route to Dedicated when you hit throughput jumps.
[02:48] Leo Park: We're also concerned about cost — tokens, storage, and ops. How does Redwood charge for embeddings + rerank?
[02:55] Maya Chen: For Hosted it's usage-based per embedding generation + per-rerank tokens if you use Redwood's model for scoring. For Dedicated you have reserved capacity and fixed GPU cost; typically lower per-token at scale but requires commit. Private is enterprise contract with platform fee. We'll send the pricing sheet.
[03:10] Dana Ortiz: What about hybrid search — combining BM25 + vector? Any best practices?
[03:15] Rajat Singh: Hybrid is common: score by BM25 to narrow to 1k or 200, then vector similarity, then optional cross-encoder. We recommend feature fusion at rerank stage: combine BM25 score, recency signals,CTR etc with vector cos sim. Redwood has hooks to surface those signals into the reranker pipeline.
[03:34] Maya Chen: Quick Q: any security or compliance blockers? SSO, SOC2, KMS?
[03:39] Sofia Ruiz: SOC2 is a must, and for certain customers we need VPC and KMS-managed keys, plus audit logs.
[03:46] Maya Chen: Redwood is SOC2 and supports KMS integrations and Private deployments into customer VPCs for air-gapped or regulated data. We'll share the compliance docs.
[03:56] Leo Park: For vector dbs, does Redwood manage sync to Pinecone or do we push?
[04:00] Rajat Singh: We integrate both ways. For Hosted many customers push embeddings to Pinecone/Weaviate and then call Redwood to generate embeddings on upload; for Dedicated we can host the vector index and provide direct, high-throughput local access — lower cross-region latency. There's sometimes confusion around "KV cache" vs "vector cache" — in our serving runtime KV cache refers to autoregressive token cache; for vectors you want index-level caching and prefetch.
[04:30] Dana Ortiz: Any limit on vector dimensionality? Like 2048 dims?
[04:34] Rajat Singh: No hard limit, but performance and storage scale roughly with dims. On GPUs you can do larger dims but indexing becomes heavier. We typically recommend 768 or 1536; if you need 2048 let's prototype in POC and evaluate memory and ANN index choice.
[04:50] Maya Chen: Let's touch on reranker model architecture — are you planning a bi-encoder + cross-encoder hybrid?
[04:55] Leo Park: Yes we do bi-encoder to compute doc vectors and a lightweight cross-encoder for final re-rank of top-20. Concerned about cross-encoder latency.
[05:05] Rajat Singh: Cross-encoders add latency; to keep within 200ms you may want to run them on Dedicated with GPU-backed low-latency SLOs or run distilled/lightweight models. Redwood supports canary rollouts so you can test quality vs latency.
[05:20] Dana Ortiz: Do you have any examples of customers who moved from Elasticsearch-only to Redwood + vector DB?
[05:25] Maya Chen: Yes, a retailer we worked with moved to hybrid — they reduced false positives by 30% and achieved lower p99 latency after index tuning. We'll share a short case study link.
[05:36] Sofia Ruiz: On the Private option, how much ops burden do we retain? We need to know the runbook for upgrades and metrics.
[05:43] Rajat Singh: Private deploys keep control with you; Redwood provides a control plane and optional managed services for upgrades and patching. You can opt for a fully managed private offering.
[05:53] Speaker 2: (inaudible) — question about cold-start for new docs and incremental indexing?
[05:58] Rajat Singh: For incremental indexing we suggest streaming embeddings on ingest to your vector DB; for new docs cold-start you can route queries to a fallback model or do on-the-fly embedding — which is slower. Redwood's routing can fall back automatically if the index is missing vectors.
[06:15] Dana Ortiz: About throughput — we aim 150 qps peak, but spikes to 300 for promotions. Can Redwood autoscale?
[06:22] Maya Chen: Dedicated pools support autoscaling and burst capacity. Hosted can also burst but with different cost characteristics. We'll include the autoscale config recommendations in the POC plan.
[06:35] Leo Park: For POC benchmark, what metrics should we capture?
[06:38] Rajat Singh: Latency (p50/p95/p99), recall/precision at k for rerank, cost per 1M queries, and throughput under concurrency. We'll produce a benchmark sheet.
[06:50] Dana Ortiz: Any gotchas integrating with our CI/CD? We prefer terraform + gitops.
[06:56] Rajat Singh: Dedicated/private infra can be managed via Terraform modules — we provide examples. Hosted is simpler for initial test.
[07:05] Sofia Ruiz: A few security questions: do you support SAML/SCIM for SSO provisioning?
[07:10] Maya Chen: Yes SAML and SCIM supported on enterprise tiers; audit logs are available.
[07:15] Leo Park: About model versions — we need version pinning for reproducibility.
[07:18] Rajat Singh: You can pin model versions in Redwood's model catalog and do canary rollouts per route.
[07:26] Dana Ortiz: Will we be able to keep embeddings on our VPC for regulated content?
[07:30] Maya Chen: Yes on Private deployments you can keep everything in your VPC and integrate your KMS. For Dedicated we also support VPC peering to isolate traffic.
[07:38] Leo Park: Regarding vector indexes, are options like IVF+PQ recommended for saving storage?
[07:42] Rajat Singh: IVF+PQ is good for large corpora to reduce memory, HNSW gives faster recall at cost of memory. With Dedicated you can tune index choice and quantization to hit latency/cost targets.
[07:56] Speaker 1: (laughs) — quick aside, the demo link you mentioned earlier?
[08:00] Maya Chen: We'll send a demo recording and a short deck with architecture patterns.
[08:05] Dana Ortiz: For the POC, what sample size do you need? We can provide 10k docs to start.
[08:09] Rajat Singh: 10k is great to validate quality and basic perf, but for indexing characteristics 100k is more representative. We'll start with 10k then scale.
[08:20] Maya Chen: Ok let's do a recap and owners.
[08:23] Maya Chen: Action items: I'll send pricing and SOC2/KMS docs; Rajat will share benchmarking plan; Leo will upload sample docs. Schedule POC week of 6/21.
[08:34] Dana Ortiz: That works. Any other questions?
[08:36] Sofia Ruiz: Not from me. Thanks everyone.
[08:38] Maya Chen: Great, thanks all. We'll follow up via email with calendar invites and the POC plan.

(Transcript truncated: faint crosstalk and short Q&A after 08:40 mark.)
